**Setting Up a New Next.js Project**

Okay, so I've got a fresh install of `node` and `npm`, perfect. Time to get a new React project going. I'll use `npx create-next-app@latest` – that's the standard, most current way. The trick is to get it to run completely non-interactively, so I don't have to sit here clicking through prompts.

My first instinct was to throw a bunch of flags at it: `npx create-next-app@latest my-app --typescript --eslint --tailwind --no-app --import-alias "@/*" --use-npm --yes`. But hold on, I don't think `--yes` is a real flag for `create-next-app`. Need to verify that. Let's check the help documentation.

Right, the basic command is just `npx create-next-app@latest`. Without any flags, it'll ask questions, which I don't want. If I do, for example `npx create-next-app@latest my-app`, it will probably use default values.

So, let's try this: `npx create-next-app@latest my-app --use-npm --typescript --eslint --tailwind --app --import-alias "@/*"`. Providing all the options should make it completely non-interactive. Now, I should make sure these are valid flags and that I haven't messed anything up. Always good to double-check the documentation to be sure.

Alright, that *should* do it. Time to run the command and see what happens.
